description: A blank ('') SEX value is a sex group of its own. Its average ratio counts in the first mean and can survive the cutoffs.

b.request: Join laboratory tests to patients by ID; compute each distinct `SEX` group’s average `CPK / GPT` over tests with a defined ratio, treating blank `SEX` as its own group. Compute the mean of all group averages, retain groups above it, then retain groups above the mean of those retained averages. Return one unrounded row containing the final groups’ mean average ratio and their mean differences from each of the two cutoff means
b.sql: WITH group_averages AS (SELECT p.SEX, AVG(1.0 * l.CPK / l.GPT) AS avg_ratio FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE l.CPK IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT IS NOT NULL AND l.GPT <> 0 GROUP BY p.SEX), first_cutoff AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS cutoff FROM group_averages), first_retained AS (SELECT g.avg_ratio FROM group_averages AS g CROSS JOIN first_cutoff AS c WHERE g.avg_ratio > c.cutoff), second_cutoff AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS cutoff FROM first_retained) SELECT AVG(g.avg_ratio) AS mean_average_ratio, AVG(g.avg_ratio - c1.cutoff) AS mean_difference_from_first_cutoff, AVG(g.avg_ratio - c2.cutoff) AS mean_difference_from_second_cutoff FROM group_averages AS g CROSS JOIN first_cutoff AS c1 CROSS JOIN second_cutoff AS c2 WHERE g.avg_ratio > c2.cutoff;

a.request: Join each lab test to its patient and compute the CPK ÷ GPT ratio per test, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Average the ratio separately for every distinct `SEX` value. Patients whose `SEX` is an empty string '' form a group of their own and are kept, and so do patients with a missing sex. Take the plain mean of all these group averages, blank group included, and keep the groups whose average is above it. Then take the mean of the kept groups' averages and keep the groups above that second mean. Return one unrounded row with: the average of the remaining groups' ratio averages, the average amount by which they exceed the first mean, and the average amount by which they exceed the second mean.
a.sql: WITH ratios AS (SELECT p.SEX, 1.0 * l.CPK / l.GPT AS ratio FROM Laboratory AS l JOIN Patient AS p ON p.ID = l.ID), group_averages AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(ratio) AS avg_ratio FROM ratios WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL GROUP BY SEX), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM group_averages), first_kept AS (SELECT g.SEX, g.avg_ratio FROM group_averages AS g CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m WHERE g.avg_ratio > m.value), second_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM first_kept) SELECT AVG(k.avg_ratio) AS average_ratio, AVG(k.avg_ratio - m1.value) AS average_above_first_mean, AVG(k.avg_ratio - m2.value) AS average_above_second_mean FROM first_kept AS k CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m1 CROSS JOIN second_mean AS m2 WHERE k.avg_ratio > m2.value

c.request: Matching lab tests to patients, average the CPK-to-GPT ratio for each `SEX` value, ignoring tests where the ratio is missing. Keep the sexes whose average is above the mean of those averages, then among them keep the ones above their own mean. In one unrounded row, give the average ratio of the sexes left, how far above the first mean they are on average, and how far above the second mean they are on average. A blank ('') SEX value is a sex group of its own. Its average ratio counts in the first mean and can survive the cutoffs.
c.sql: WITH sex_averages AS (SELECT p.SEX, AVG(1.0 * l.CPK / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM sex_averages), first_cut AS (SELECT s.SEX, s.avg_ratio FROM sex_averages AS s CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m WHERE s.avg_ratio > m.value), second_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM first_cut), second_cut AS (SELECT f.avg_ratio FROM first_cut AS f CROSS JOIN second_mean AS m WHERE f.avg_ratio > m.value) SELECT AVG(s.avg_ratio) AS average_ratio, AVG(s.avg_ratio - f.value) AS average_above_first_mean, AVG(s.avg_ratio - m.value) AS average_above_second_mean FROM second_cut AS s CROSS JOIN first_mean AS f CROSS JOIN second_mean AS m;

d.request: Match lab tests to patients and calculate the average CPK-to-GPT ratio for each `SEX` value, ignoring tests with a missing ratio. Treat a blank (`''`) `SEX` value as its own group: include its average in the mean of the group averages and allow it to pass the cutoffs. Keep the groups whose averages exceed that first mean, then keep those whose averages exceed the mean of the remaining groups. In one unrounded row, report the average ratio of the final groups, their average distance above the first mean, and their average distance above the second mean.
d.sql: WITH group_averages AS (SELECT p.SEX, AVG(1.0 * l.CPK / NULLIF(l.GPT, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.SEX), first_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM group_averages), first_pass AS (SELECT g.avg_ratio FROM group_averages AS g CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m WHERE g.avg_ratio > m.value), second_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) AS value FROM first_pass) SELECT AVG(f.avg_ratio) AS average_ratio, AVG(f.avg_ratio - m1.value) AS average_above_first_mean, AVG(f.avg_ratio - m2.value) AS average_above_second_mean FROM first_pass AS f CROSS JOIN first_mean AS m1 CROSS JOIN second_mean AS m2 WHERE f.avg_ratio > m2.value;
